data.long_meaning: In Late Latin, Agnès is derived from the word agnus, which means 'lamb'. This name is popular among Christians as a symbol of purity and innocence. Agnès is the feminine form of the name Agnes, which was given to early Christian martyrs who were sentenced to be buried alive in a jar of honey. In the Middle Ages, Agnès was also a popular name for noblewomen.
